# 1 Clement Chapter 59 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 59 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_059_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 59

*[The Great Prayer — Part I: Opening Address and Petition for Illumination]*

**59:1** But if certain persons should be disobedient to what has been said by him through us, let them know that they will entangle themselves in transgression and no small danger; but we shall be innocent of this sin, and we will ask with earnest prayer and supplication that the Creator of all may keep intact the fixed number of his elect throughout the whole world, through his beloved child Jesus Christ, through whom he called us from darkness to light, from ignorance to the knowledge of the glory of his name.

**59:2** Grant us to hope upon your name, which is the beginning of all creation — open the eyes of our hearts to know you, you who alone are Highest among the highest, Holy resting among the holy; you who humble the insolence of the proud, who scatter the counsels of the nations, who exalt the humble and abase the exalted; you who make rich and make poor; you who kill and make alive, you who alone are the Finder of spirits and the God of all flesh; you who look upon the depths, you who oversee the works of men; the Helper of those in danger, the Savior of those in despair; the Creator and Keeper of every spirit; you who multiply the nations upon the earth, and out of all you have chosen those who love you through Jesus Christ, your beloved child; through whom you have disciplined us, sanctified us, and honored us.

**59:3** We beseech you, Master, to be our helper and defender. Those among us who are in affliction — save them; those who are lowly — raise up; those who have fallen — lift up; the sick — heal; the wandering ones of your people — turn back; the hungry ones — feed; the captives — release; the feeble — strengthen; the faint-hearted — take courage. Let all the nations know you, that you alone are God, and that Jesus Christ is your child, and that we are your people and the sheep of your pasture.

---

*EMET renders the Greek of Codex Alexandrinus with maximal literalness. Chapter 59 opens the Great Prayer (chs. 59–61), one of the earliest extant Christian liturgical prayers.*
